input_summary: Two content sections: (1) Items ~551-600 KÜLTÜREL ŞOKLAR — Cultural upheaval, invasions, transitions, modernization shocks; (2) Items ~601-700 BOZKIR FELSEFESİ — Nomadic philosophy, steppe worldview, ethics, aesthetics.

candidates.title: Transgenerational Trauma and Steppe Invasions: How Eurasian Nomadic Societies Encoded Collective Memory
candidates.central_question: How did major invasions (Mongol, Turkic, Russian expansions) create measurable psychological and social ruptures that persisted across generations in Turkic and steppe communities?
candidates.geography: Eurasian steppe, Turkic territories, Central Asia, Caucasus
known_sources_seen: Frontiers psychiatry article on collective trauma in Eastern Europe
Prevention Institute historical & cultural trauma framework
Academic literature on transgenerational trauma mechanisms
candidates.research_risk: medium — archival evidence of psychological impact is indirect (material culture, oral tradition, organizational collapse); requires careful inference from economic/social data
candidates.video_proposal: Documentary-style; interview historians on trauma codification; visual metaphors of cyclical displacement; archival maps of migration waves

candidates.title: From Sacred Hierarchy to Egalitarian Shock: How Steppe Communities Negotiated Sedentary State Pressure (1600-1900)
candidates.central_question: What specific mechanisms did nomadic Turkic societies use to resist or adapt to sedentarization pressure, and how did this reshape their ethical codes and social contracts?
candidates.geography: Ottoman borders, Russian frontier, Caucasus, Central Asia
known_sources_seen: Ottoman Enlightenment literature (medical school debates on reform)
Young Ottomans secret society records
Russian-Caucasus frontier archives
candidates.research_risk: low — primary sources exist (Ottoman records, Caucasian tribal archives, ethnographic observations); risk is interpretation (reading adaptation vs. forced assimilation from different angles)
candidates.video_proposal: Historical reenactment segments showing council deliberations; montage of material culture adaptation; expert commentary on ethical paradigm shifts

candidates.title: Modernization Shock and Lost Literacy: How 19th-Century Turkic Communities Faced Script and Language Displacement
candidates.central_question: What was the actual lived experience of Turkic speakers as Arabic script was questioned, Latin script emerged, and Cyrillic was imposed — and how did this linguistic rupture reshape cultural identity?
candidates.geography: Ottoman Empire, Caucasus, Central Asia, Soviet Union
known_sources_seen: Ottoman Enlightenment reform literature on education
Atatürk reforms documentation
Soviet linguistic policy archives
candidates.research_risk: low — primary sources abundant (decree texts, educational records, personal writings); potential myth: that this was a smooth 'progress' rather than genuine cultural rupture
candidates.video_proposal: Visual transformation of text; archive footage of school scenes; elderly testimony on script transition; calligraphy sequences showing the shift

candidates.title: Tengrism as a Unifying Philosophical System: The Epistemology of Steppe Societies and Their Relation to Power
candidates.central_question: What were the core epistemological principles of Tengrism (worship of eternal sky, Tengri) and how did this framework structure decision-making, ethics, and political legitimacy across nomadic Turkic and Mongolic societies?
candidates.period: Antiquity-16th century (with long continuities to present)
candidates.geography: Eurasian steppe, Turkic heartlands, Mongolia, Central Asia
known_sources_seen: Academia.edu: Steppe Nomads as Philosophical Problem in Classical China
Eurasian nomads overview (grokipedia) on Tengrism
Academic sources on nomadic religious philosophy
candidates.research_risk: medium — primary sources are fragmentary (Chinese chronicles describing 'barbarian' beliefs, Islamic sources hostile to 'pagan' systems, later ethnographic accounts); requires careful de-centering of hostile observers' framing
candidates.video_proposal: Animated cosmology diagram of Tengri concept; archaeological evidence of ritual spaces; expert interviews on animism vs. monotheism debate; visual metaphor of sky as political symbol

candidates.title: The Ethics of Perpetual Movement: Honor, Duty, and Self-Reliance as Nomadic Philosophical Archetypes
candidates.central_question: How did the material reality of constant steppe mobility translate into a coherent ethical system centered on Honor, Duty, and Loyalty, and how did this differ fundamentally from sedentary moral philosophy?
candidates.geography: Turkic-Mongolian steppe societies, Central Asia, Caucasus
known_sources_seen: Academic sources on Turkic-Mongolian ethics and military archetypes
Bowdoin course: Ethics in the Steppe (Kazakh nature-culture connection)
Ethnographic literature on nomadic value systems
candidates.research_risk: low — rich material culture, oral traditions, and historical chronicles provide direct evidence of these values; risk is avoiding romanticization vs. using critical source analysis
candidates.video_proposal: Portrait-style interviews with contemporary steppe philosophers; reenactment of council deliberations showing honor codes; visual metaphor of 'endless horizon' as ethical framework; comparative animation with sedentary societies

candidates.title: Space as Sacred: The Metaphysics of Steppe Ecology and Nomadic Environmental Philosophy
candidates.central_question: How did nomadic steppe cultures encode space itself — pasture, horizon, migration routes, sacred geography — into a coherent metaphysical worldview, and how did this contrast with sedentary place-based philosophies?
candidates.geography: Great Steppe, Central Asian watersheds, migration corridors
known_sources_seen: Academia.edu: The Idea of Space among the Nomads of Great Steppe
Yale Steppelands 2.0 working group on philosophical geography
Sociostudies journal article on spatial worldview of nomads
candidates.research_risk: high — primary sources for pre-Islamic steppe metaphysics are mediated through hostile/outsider observers (Chinese, Islamic, later European chronicles); requires sophisticated source criticism and careful epistemological humility
candidates.video_proposal: Aerial steppe cinematography; animated migration maps layered with mythological significance; expert interviews on nomadic ontology; archaeological site visits to sacred locations; visual translation of 'space-as-ethics'

candidates.title: The Aesthetics of Impermanence: How Nomadic Material Culture Encoded Philosophical Principles
candidates.central_question: What can the design, ornamentation, and ephemeral nature of nomadic material culture (yurts, textiles, tools, decorative arts) tell us about the underlying aesthetic philosophy and values of steppe societies?
candidates.geography: Eurasian steppe, Turkic and Mongolian territories
known_sources_seen: Ethnographic museum collections and catalogs
Craft tradition documentation
Archaeological evidence of portable housing and textiles
candidates.research_risk: low — material evidence is abundant and directly observable; contemporary craftspeople carry living traditions; museums hold extensive collections; risk is interpretive (avoiding projection of modern aesthetics onto historical choices)
candidates.video_proposal: Museum field work; artisan workshops showing traditional techniques; close-up cinematography of textile patterns and yurt architecture; animation showing design principles; expert analysis of functional aesthetics

meta.next_step: User selects one or more candidates per section. Selected candidates proceed to Phase B (Deep Research). Unselected candidates archived for future consideration.
meta.notes: Web search completed for all three queries. Candidates grouped by section with varying novelty/evidence balance. KÜLTÜREL ŞOKLAR candidates emphasize primary source availability and historiographical depth; BOZKIR FELSEFESİ candidates emphasize interpretive complexity and 'lost source' recovery.
